1	# Hybrid Simulator User Guide
2	
3	Audience: a new engineer who wants to RUN the Andes hybrid simulator,
4	not study its internals. After this guide you can:
5	
6	1. Build every artifact from a fresh clone.
7	2. Configure QEMU, vsim, and the driver for a workload.
8	3. Pick a switching mode (marker or PC) and run one handoff end-to-end
9	   with a concrete worked example.
10	
11	For per-mode drill-down, read `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md`.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## 0. The one-paragraph mental model
16	
17	QEMU runs the boring parts at MHz. vsim (Verilator + SystemC) runs the
18	small region-of-interest at cycle accuracy. They share RAM via an
19	`mmap` file. A magic trigger (marker HINT or PC)
20	hands control between them. One run is two legs:
21	
22	```
23	   QEMU1  -- state.bin + shared mmap -->  vsim
24	   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)
25	```
26	
27	The thing you choose per run is the TRIGGER that decides where each
28	leg drains and the next leg resumes. That choice is the "switching
29	mode".
30	
31	---
32	
33	## 0.5 Quick start with `./andesim`
34	
35	`./andesim` is the canonical end-user entry point (the C++ driver; it
36	self-builds on first use). It drives `run` itself, orchestrating QEMU and
37	vsim directly; building is done by `scripts/build_all.sh` (which delegates to
38	`setup.sh`, `scripts/build_*.sh`). Sections 1-7 document those underlying
39	scripts (`tests/e2e.sh`, `scripts/run_e2e.sh`) for when you need to bypass
40	the driver.
41	
42	Four-command worked example - cold checkout to passing suite:
43	
44	```sh
45	bash scripts/build_all.sh                             # qemu, vsim, plugin, fixtures
46	./andesim list engines                                # discover the built engines
47	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
48	  tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf                         # one marker-mode handoff
49	JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh                          # the hybrid e2e suite (or scripts/test_all.sh for unit+contract+e2e)
50	```
51	
52	Expected last line of `scripts/run_e2e.sh`:
53	
54	```
55	summary: marker <N>p/0f/<S>s  pc <N>p/0f/<S>s  neg <N>p/0f/0s  total <N> passed, 0 failed, <S> skipped
56	```
57	
58	Subcommand cheat sheet:
59	
60	| Command                                                          | What it does                                                        |
61	|------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
62	| `./andesim list <models|engines>`                              | List the 3 models, or the discovered engines with their hardware params (XLEN/VLEN/DLEN/ELEN; `-` = not reported). |
63	| `bash scripts/build_all.sh [TARGET] [--dry-run]`               | Build artifacts; targets: `all`, `plugin`, `fixtures`, `runtime` (qemu and vsim are external prebuilt binaries, not built here). |
64	| `./andesim doctor`                                             | Read-only environment health check: artifacts, submodules, toolchain, runtime, discovered engines, and `/dev/shm` mmap tiers (with WSL2 advice). |
65	| `./andesim run --mode fast|cycle|hybrid [--trigger marker|pc] [--engine ID] [--gdb [--gdb-port PORT]] <elf>` | Run one ELF on a model (hybrid = QEMU -> vsim handoff and REQUIRES `--trigger marker|pc` to delimit the ROI; --gdb pauses at startup for a debugger: fast opens QEMU's GDB stub on port 1234, cycle halts the hart and opens vsim's JTAG port (9104) then execs `$ICEMAN`, a GDB server (use a modern OpenOCD); --gdb not supported with hybrid). |
66	| `bash scripts/run_e2e.sh` (env: `FILTER`, `MODE`, `JOBS`)        | Run the hybrid e2e suite directly (qemu+vsim round-trips). |
67	| `bash scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit\|contract\|e2e]`     | Run the full test surface: C++ unit tests + driver contracts + the e2e suite. |
68	
69	Run `./andesim <cmd> -h` for the full flag list of a subcommand (set
70	`ANDESIM_DEV=1` to reveal developer-only flags and the `list fixtures`
71	target). The rest of this guide (Sections 1-7) documents the
72	underlying scripts and is useful when you need to bypass `./andesim`
73	(custom env vars, single-leg debugging, alternative CPU YAML, etc.).
74	
75	---
76	
77	## 1. Build and environment setup
78	
79	### 1.1 Host prerequisites
80	
81	Install these on the host once:
82	
83	| Package          | Notes                                                |
84	|------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
85	| `git`            | clone the repo and its submodules                    |
86	| C/C++ toolchain  | clang or gcc; needed by QEMU and the plugin          |
87	| `cmake` >= 3.20  | vsim build                                           |
88	| `ninja`          | vsim default generator                               |
89	| `python3`        | plugin tests, engine deriver scripts                 |
90	| `glib-2.0` dev   | QEMU plugin link line                                |
91	| `pkg-config`     | plugin build (glib-2.0)                              |
92	| `podman`         | runs vsim builds inside `vsim-env:latest` container  |
93	| Verilator        | auto-detected; set `VSIM_VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE` if needed |
94	| QEMU             | prebuilt external binary; set `QEMU_BIN_DIR` (not built here) |
95	| RISC-V toolchain | `riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,nm,objdump}` (Andes v5d)   |
96	
97	The Andes RISC-V toolchain is needed to build the fixtures and to
98	resolve symbols for PC-mode. The harness scripts default to
99	`/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/.../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`;
100	override with `NM=/your/path/to/nm` if you keep it elsewhere.
101	
102	### 1.2 Clone with submodules
103	
104	```sh
105	git clone --recursive https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim
106	cd hybrid_sim
107	```
108	
109	If you forgot `--recursive`:
110	
111	```sh
112	git submodule update --init --recursive
113	```
114	
115	Submodules under this repo:
116	
117	| Path             | What it is                                          |
118	|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
119	| `include/`     | the shared ABI (`andesim_abi` repo): `hybrid_state_v1` wire contract under `include/hybrid/` |
120	
121	vsim is no longer a submodule -- it is a prebuilt **external** binary, like QEMU.
122	Build it in your own vsim (`hybrid_vsim`) checkout and point `VSIM_BIN_DIR`
123	(`config.env`) at its `build/` dir; see 1.3.
124	
125	### 1.3 Per-host config (`config.env`)
126	
127	The repo ships a template `config.env.example` listing per-host paths
128	that cannot live in the build system (notably the Andes RISC-V
129	toolchain root, which `setup.sh` does NOT build).
130	
131	On the first `source ./setup.sh`, the template is copied to
132	`./config.env` (gitignored) so your edits never touch git history. If
133	the toolchain lives somewhere other than the default, edit
134	`config.env`:
135	
136	```sh
137	# config.env
138	HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d
139	HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds32le-elf-newlib-v5d
140	```
141	
142	The variables today:
143	
144	| Variable            | What it points at                                                  |
145	|---------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
146	| `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN`  | rv64 toolchain root. `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/` must contain `riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,ld,nm,objdump,...}`. |
147	| `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32`| rv32 toolchain root (a *separate* install), for building the rv32 runtime + fixtures. `bin/` must contain `riscv32-unknown-elf-{gcc,ar,...}`. Optional: leave unset if you only target rv64 (rv32 builds are skipped). |
148	| `QEMU_BIN_DIR`      | External prebuilt QEMU build dir holding `qemu-system-riscv64` AND `qemu-system-riscv32` (this repo no longer builds QEMU). |
149	| `VSIM_BIN_DIR`      | External prebuilt vsim build dir holding the `sim_*` binaries (this repo no longer builds vsim; the driver discovers cycle engines by scanning it). |
150	
151	How it propagates:
152	
153	- `setup.sh` sources `config.env`, validates `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/`
154	  exists, and `export`s the variable so all child processes see it.
155	- The fixture `Makefile` (`tests/fixtures/Makefile`) defaults
156	  `TOOLCHAIN` to `$(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)` and aborts with a clear error if
157	  the variable is missing.
158	- The unified `e2e.sh` test harness loads `config.env` itself when run
159	  without prior `source ./setup.sh`, then derives
160	  `NM=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`.
161	
162	Override per-invocation without editing the file:
163	
164	```sh
165	HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/my-toolchain make -C tests/fixtures
166	HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/my-toolchain ./andesim run \
167	  tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
168	  --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x<post-jal>  # see docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md
169	```
170	
171	### 1.4 Build everything
172	
173	One command builds all three artifacts and exports the env vars the
174	test harness expects:
175	
176	```sh
177	source ./setup.sh
178	```
179	
180	`source` (not `bash`) is required so the script can prepend the build
181	dirs to PATH and export `VSIM_QEMU`, `VSIM_PLUGIN`, `VSIM_BIN_DIR`,
182	`QEMU_BIN_DIR`, `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` into the current shell. The steps it
183	runs:
184	
185	```
186	0/3 config     -> auto-copy config.env.example -> config.env (first run);
187	                  source it; export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN + QEMU_BIN_DIR + VSIM_BIN_DIR
188	1/3 QEMU       -> located (external prebuilt): $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64
189	2/3 vsim       -> located (external prebuilt): $VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_*
190	3/3 plugin     -> qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
191	```
192	
193	Neither QEMU nor vsim is built here: build each in its own checkout and point
194	`QEMU_BIN_DIR` / `VSIM_BIN_DIR` (in `config.env`) at the dirs holding
195	`qemu-system-riscv64` / the `sim_*` binaries.
196	
197	To rebuild the one component this repo still builds:
198	
199	```sh
200	make -C qemu_plugin            # plugins; vendored qemu-plugin.h, no QEMU source needed
201	```
202	
203	(vsim is rebuilt in your external vsim checkout via its own `build_vsim.sh`.)
204	
205	To clean:
206	
207	```sh
208	source ./setup.sh clean         # both
209	source ./setup.sh clean vsim
210	source ./setup.sh clean plugin
211	```
212	
213	### 1.5 Build the test fixtures (RISC-V ELFs)
214	
215	Fixtures are small RISC-V programs that exercise specific transport
216	paths. They are NOT built by `setup.sh`; build them once:
217	
218	```sh
219	make -C tests/fixtures -j
220	```
221	
222	One fixture at a time:
223	
224	```sh
225	make -C tests/fixtures rt_c_v_matmul.elf
226	```
227	
228	Output ELFs land next to the sources under
229	`tests/fixtures/*.elf`. The fixtures depend on the Andes
230	RISC-V GCC (newlib); all C fixtures link through the vplat runtime
231	(section 5), so no semihosting library is involved. The toolchain path
232	comes from `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` (see section 1.3); to override for one
233	invocation:
234	
235	```sh
236	make -C tests/fixtures TOOLCHAIN=/opt/my-toolchain
237	```
238	
239	### 1.6 Sanity check the build
240	
241	```sh
242	# Artifacts present? (QEMU is external -- set via QEMU_BIN_DIR)
243	ls "$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64"
244	ls "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/sim_ax45mpv_premium
245	ls qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
246	
247	# Smallest possible end-to-end - one marker-mode handoff:
248	FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TRIGGER_MODE=marker TIMEOUT=120 \
249	  bash tests/e2e.sh
250	```
251	
252	Expected last line:
253	
254	```
255	[rt_c_v_matmul PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)
256	```
257	
258	If you see `skip: ... not built`, redo `source ./setup.sh` and
259	re-build fixtures (`make -C tests/fixtures`).
260	
261	---
262	
263	## 2. Configuring the simulator
264	
265	There are four configuration surfaces. Most users only touch the env
266	vars in 2.1.
267	
268	### 2.1 Environment variables (the only ones you usually set)
269	
270	`setup.sh` exports these for you. Override only if your artifacts live
271	somewhere non-default.
272

325	### 2.3 QEMU plugin args
326	
327	The plugin reads `arg=value` tokens after `-plugin <path>,`. They
328	select WHICH switching mode QEMU1 runs in:
329	
330	| Plugin arg           | Effect                                                                 |
331	|----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
332	| `outfile=PATH`       | REQUIRED. Drained `hybrid_state_v1` is written here.                   |
333	| `enter_pc=0xADDR`    | PC mode: drain when PC == ADDR. Bypasses the marker-insn matcher.         |
334	| `exit_marker=1`      | Oracle exit drain (verification): arm on the EXIT marker `slti x0,x0,0x5A1`, drain right after it retires. The run never hands off -- it produces the reference state `--verify` compares against. Exclusive with the other mode args. |
335	| `exit_pc=0xADDR`     | Oracle exit drain, pc form: arm when PC == ADDR instead of on the exit marker. |
336	| `drain_pc=0xADDR`    | Oracle modifier: after arming, drain at the first hit of ADDR (the verifier passes vsim's drained pc here, so both sides sample the same architectural point -- vsim's DMI halt lands a few insns past the trigger). |
337	| `ilm_size=BYTES`, `dlm_size=BYTES` | LM content transport: additionally drain that many bytes of ILM/DLM content (read through the hart-0 local-memory slave ports) into raw sidecar files `<outfile>.ilm` / `<outfile>.dlm`. Default 0 = skip (engine without that local memory); the driver passes the paired engine's sizes. |
338	| `ilm_base=0xADDR`, `dlm_base=0xADDR` | Override the LM slave-port bases (defaults `0xA0000000` / `0xA0200000`, AE350 hart 0). |
339	| `hvm_size=BYTES`     | HVM content transport: drain that many bytes of the High-Bandwidth Vector Memory into `<outfile>.hvm`, same contract as the LM sidecars. Default 0 = skip. |
340	| `hvm_base=0xADDR`    | Override the HVM subordinate-port base (default `0x90000000`, AE350). |
341	
342	If no mode arg is given, the default is marker-insn match (marker mode): the
343	plugin matches `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` at retire.

352	
353	`sim_ax45mpv_premium <elf> [flags]`. The hybrid-relevant subset:
354	
355	| Flag                          | Purpose                                                  |
356	|-------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
357	| `--resume-from-qemu FILE`     | Read drained state, restore into hart, run from PC.     |
358	| `--handoff-out FILE`          | Drain back into FILE when the exit trigger fires.       |
359	| `--shared-mem-path FILE`      | mmap FILE as RAM (zero-copy share with QEMU).           |
360	| `--shared-mem-size BYTES`     | Size of the shared region. Match QEMU `-m`.             |
361	| `--shared-mem-base HEX`       | Guest physical address where file offset 0 lands.       |
362	| `--hybrid-exit-pc 0xADDR`     | PC mode exit: drain when this PC retires.               |
363	| `--drain-minimal`             | Exit drain reads back only mcycle/minstret; the driver sets it when `--verify` is off. |
364	| `--no-reset-baseline`         | Disable the liveness gate (below): restore every transported register. |
365	| `--jtag-port N`               | Open the JTAG bitbang port (ICEman or OpenOCD). The hart free-runs; the debugger halts it over the JTAG DTM on connect. The `./andesim run --mode cycle --gdb` path opens this port for ICEman (set `$ICEMAN`). |

367	
368	`--shared-mem-base` must be the guest physical address of RAM: `0x0` on the
369	`andes_ae350` machine (its DRAM window is `0x0..0x7fffffff`; `0x80000000` is
370	the boot MROM, and vsim's built-in `0x80000000` default targets the upstream
371	`virt` machine). The driver always passes `0x0`; only standalone vsim
372	invocations need to override it.
373	
374	**Liveness gate (reset baseline).** Every register moved through the Debug
375	Module costs hundreds of simulated cycles, and most transported state still
376	holds its reset value. So the resume skips any restore whose drained value
377	equals the engine's own reset value -- a no-op write. The very first hybrid
378	run of a given (engine build, ELF) pair drains that reset state once (a few
379	extra seconds) and caches it under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/` (fallback
380	`~/.cache/andesim/`); later runs load the cache and typically cut the vsim
381	leg by ~4x (hello: 50k -> 12k simulated cycles). The cache self-invalidates
382	on engine rebuild or ELF change (mtime+size keyed); delete the directory to
383	force a fresh capture. `--verify` works unchanged with the gate active;
384	`--no-reset-baseline` restores the old transport-everything behavior.
385	
386	Run `$VSIM_BIN --help` for the full list (waveform/save/restore are
387	license-gated and off by default).

389	### 2.5 Requesting memory (`--mem-size` + `HSIM_MMAP_DIR`)
390	
391	By default every `./andesim` invocation that needs a shared mmap allocates
392	a 128 MiB sparse file under `/dev/shm` (tmpfs, RAM-backed). When your
393	workload's memory footprint exceeds `/dev/shm` capacity (typically
394	RAM/2 on Linux), two knobs let you redirect:
395	
396	| Knob              | Where             | What it does |
397	|-------------------|-------------------|--------------|
398	| `--mem-size SPEC` | flag on `run` (`--mmap-size` is the old alias) | request guest program memory (`SPEC` = `128M`, `1.5G`, `2G`, or raw bytes). Cap `2G` minus one 4 KiB V-transport page (the AE350 DRAM window). |
399	| `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/path` | env var | pin the backing directory (skips the tier list below). |
400	
401	Per-model semantics of `--mem-size`:
402	
403	| Model    | What it does |
404	|----------|--------------|
405	| `hybrid` | `--mem-size` is your **program** RAM (default `128M`). The driver maps one extra 4 KiB page on top for the V-register transport scratch (L26): the physical shared mmap = QEMU memory backend = vsim RAM window = `--mem-size + 4 KiB`, with the scratch parked in that top page, just above everything your program can address. You get your full `--mem-size`; the page is invisible. The driver rejects `> 2G - 4 KiB` **before** allocating, and rejects an ELF whose static image would extend into the reserved page (`raise --mem-size`). |
406	| `fast`   | forwards a plain QEMU `-m`. Without the flag the argv is untouched -- QEMU as-is, its own 128 MiB default, no mmap involved. No `2G` cap here (that ceiling is the hybrid shared-mmap window, not fast's); QEMU itself validates the size and rejects only oversized values (`Cannot model more than 16GB RAM` on the AE350 machine). |
407	| `cycle`  | validate-only: the cycle engine always models its full DRAM window, so there is nothing to size (the driver says so on stderr). |
408	
409	Backing-directory selection (`./andesim`): a two-tier list, first fit
410	wins (fit = size + 256 MiB free):
411	
412	1. `/dev/shm` -- tmpfs, RAM speed. Skipped when absent or too small.
413	2. `~/.cache/andesim` (honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`) -- disk-backed; the
414	   size ceiling becomes disk free space. Hot pages still sit in the
415	   kernel page cache, so the cost vs tmpfs is background writeback only.
416	
417	We never switch **silently**: the status line always names the chosen
418	dir, and a fallback adds the reason, e.g.
419	`[hsim mmap] 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andesim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))`.
420	`HSIM_MMAP_DIR` pins a single dir with **no** fallback past it: rc=2
421	with a hint if it can't hold the request.
422	
423	Examples:
424	
425	```sh
426	# Small request; /dev/shm fits, so tier 1 is chosen.
427	./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 256M
428	#   [hsim mmap] 256.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 252.0 GiB)
429	
430	# Near-max request on a small-RAM box: falls through to the disk tier,
431	# and the status line says so. (2047M is the hybrid ceiling -- exactly 2G is
432	# rejected because the extra V-scratch page would overflow the DRAM window.)
433	./andesim run my.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 2047M
434	#   [hsim mmap] 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andesim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))
435	
436	# Pin a scratch filesystem instead (no fallback past the pin):
437	HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/scratch \
438	  ./andesim run my.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 2047M
439	```
440	
441	If you pin `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/tmp` and `/tmp` is mounted as tmpfs (Arch
442	default), that does not lift the RAM ceiling; pick a directory on a
443	non-tmpfs filesystem (`/var/tmp`, `/scratch`, etc.) -- or just let the
444	tier list pick `~/.cache/andesim` for you.
445	
446	The hardcoded `mktemp -p /dev/shm` paths in the shell harnesses
447	(`tests/e2e.sh`, `tests/drivers/*.sh`, `tests/plugin/*.sh`) all use
448	128 MiB and are unaffected.

450	### 2.5.1 Running on WSL2 and macOS
451	
452	The hybrid handoff needs both legs (QEMU and vsim) on **one Linux
453	kernel**, with the mmap file on a filesystem local to that kernel.
454	That rule decides what each OS needs:
455	
456	**Linux** -- native, nothing to do.
457	
458	**Windows (WSL2)** -- works as Linux; two caveats:
459	
460	- Keep the repo and the mmap dirs on the ext4 side (`~/...`), never
461	  under `/mnt/c` (drvfs is slow and `MAP_SHARED` is not coherent there).
462	- `/dev/shm` is capped by the WSL VM memory. Raise `memory=` in
463	  `%UserProfile%\.wslconfig` if tier 1 is too small -- or just let the
464	  tier list fall through to `~/.cache/andesim`.
465	
466	`./andesim doctor` checks both (see the `mmap tiers:` section and the
467	WSL warnings at the end of its report).
468	
469	**macOS** -- run-only. vsim is a Linux binary, so `./andesim` re-execs
470	the run inside a prebuilt Linux runtime image in the podman machine VM;
471	the mmap lives inside that VM (the container's `/dev/shm`), never on a
472	virtiofs mount. One-time setup:
473	
474	```sh
475	brew install podman
476	podman machine init --memory 4096   # the VM hosts /dev/shm (tier 1)
477	podman machine start
478	podman pull <runtime image>         # or load a CI-built andesim-runtime:latest
479	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --mem-size 256M my.elf

483	`ANDESIM_SHM_SIZE` (container `/dev/shm`, default `3g`),
484	`ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE` (podman/docker). Your current directory is

491	### 2.6 The hybrid guest memory map (`--print-memmap`)
492	
493	Which addresses may a hybrid workload touch? Print the map for exactly the
494	run you are about to do (same `--engine` / `--mem-size`; the ELF is optional
495	and only adds a fit note):
496	
497	```sh
498	./andesim run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 128M
499	```
500	
501	```
502	REGION           BASE         END          SIZE    TRANSPORT
503	DRAM             0x0          0x7ffffff    128M    shared mmap; content survives the handoff
504	V-scratch        0x8000000    0x8000fff    4K      reserved by the hybrid V transport; not program-usable
505	ILM              0x0          0xffff       64K     sidecar .ilm; DRAM overlay while milmb.IEN=1
506	DLM              0x200000     0x207fff     32K     sidecar .dlm; DRAM overlay while mdlmb.IEN=1
507	HVM              0x90000000   0x9003ffff   256K    sidecar .hvm
508	SimControl/HTIF  0xe0080000   0xe0080fff   4K      device; state does not cross the handoff
509	UART2            0xf0300000   0xf03fffff   1M      device (console); state does not cross the handoff
510	```
511	
512	Reading the table:
513	
514	- **END is the inclusive last byte**; SIZE is the region span.
515	- **DRAM** tracks `--mem-size`; the **V-scratch** page above it belongs to
516	  the V-register transport (2.5) -- the driver rejects an ELF that reaches
517	  into it.
518	- **ILM/DLM/HVM** rows appear only when the engine can actually transport
519	  their content (`--describe` sizes > 0, the backdoor gate); their bases come
520	  from the engine's own `--print-qemu-config` geometry -- the same file the
521	  QEMU leg boots with -- so the printed map IS the run's effective one.
522	- **Devices**: only the vplat set both engines model is listed. Device STATE
523	  never crosses the handoff (each engine has its own UART/SimControl
524	  instance); only RAM content does.
525	- Anything NOT in the table is unsupported in hybrid mode: it is modeled by
526	  one engine only (QEMU's PLIC/PLMT/MROM/virtio..., vsim's debug-module
527	  window), so touching it inside the ROI gives engine-specific behavior.
528	
529	The map is hybrid-only surface: `--mode fast|cycle` run one engine's native
530	map, which the driver does not model (`--print-memmap` errors there). vsim's
531	own `--print-memmap` dumps its interconnect routing table -- useful for
532	engine bring-up, but it is one engine's view, not the hybrid contract;
533	`tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_print_memmap.sh` cross-checks the two so they
534	cannot drift apart.

538	## 3. Switching modes - which trigger to use
539	
540	| Mode     | Profiles          | Switch boundary                                          | Cycle figure           |
541	|----------|-------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|------------------------|
542	| marker   | a kernel          | `slti x0,x0,0x5A0/1` insn match (markers in source)         | kernel cycles          |
543	| PC       | a kernel          | PC equals a boundary: any symbol or `0x` address (both `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` required) | kernel cycles |
544	
545	Marker/PC delimit ONE kernel you choose. Both go through `./andesim run
546	--mode hybrid --trigger marker|pc`. The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle`
547	delta.
548	
549	Decision flow:
550	
551	```
552	Profiling ONE region you can name (a kernel)?
553	  binary is yours to edit          -> marker (andesim_ROI_begin()/end() around it)
554	  not editable, symbol/PC at ends  -> PC   (./andesim run --mode hybrid
555	                                            --trigger pc --pc-start S --pc-end E)
556	```
557	
558	**Hardware-config sync.** A hybrid run models ONE core on two engines, so
559	the QEMU fast leg inherits the selected engine's hardware config. Three
560	things flow from engine to QEMU, all derived from the engine's frozen
561	`config.inc`:
562	
563	- **VLEN** comes from the engine's `--describe` (512 when the engine
564	  reports none) and shows in the run banner as `vlen=N`.
565	- **The ISA** (extensions: CoDense, Zfh, Zba/Zbb/Zbc/Zbs, `xandesv5isa`,
566	  ...) comes from the engine's `--print-qemu-config`: the driver captures
567	  that QEMU `-readconfig` cfg and hands it to the fast leg, so QEMU executes
568	  the same extensions the engine models instead of a fixed `-cpu` string.
569	  An engine built without the flag (an older binary) makes the driver fall
570	  back to its default `-cpu` with no error. See `docs/qemu_match_ROADMAP.md`.
571	- **ILM/DLM content** (`--describe` `ilm_size`/`dlm_size`, bytes): when the
572	  engine has local memories, the fast leg's plugin also drains their content
573	  into `<state>.ilm`/`.dlm` sidecar files and the vsim leg loads them back
574	  (`--ilm`/`--dlm`), so a program that stages code/data in TCM before the ROI
575	  resumes with that content in place. An engine without local memories (or an
576	  older binary that does not report them) adds nothing. A guest that uses TCM
577	  must enable it itself (write `milmb`/`mdlmb`) -- which real TCM firmware
578	  does anyway; that CSR write rides the v6 write-mask so the enable is
579	  restored on the vsim leg. See `ROADMAP_ilm_dlm.md`.
580	- **HVM content** (`--describe` `hvm_size`, bytes): same contract for the
581	  High-Bandwidth Vector Memory at `0x90000000` -- the plugin drains
582	  `<state>.hvm`, the vsim leg backdoor-loads it (`--hvm`), and the exit
583	  drain dumps it back next to the handoff-out state. A program that stages
584	  vector data in HVM before the ROI resumes with that data in place; there
585	  is no enable bit (the geometry CSRs `mhvm_cfg`/`mhvmb` are read-only
586	  constants both sides derive from the same config). See `ROADMAP_hvm.md`.
587	
588	An engine whose XLEN is not 64 (e.g. `vsim:d23`, rv32) cannot share
589	architectural state with the rv64 fast leg and is rejected with a clear
590	error.
591	
592	**Preview the commands (`--dry-run`).** Add `--dry-run` to **any** mode
593	(`fast`, `cycle`, or `hybrid`) to print the exact engine command line(s) --
594	fully resolved and shell-quoted, including any matched `-readconfig` and all
595	paths -- and run nothing. `fast`/`cycle` print their single standalone command;
596	`hybrid` prints both legs:
597	
598	```
599	./andesim run --mode fast --dry-run prog.elf
600	# [andesim] dry-run: 1 command(s), not executed
601	# # command 1/1: standalone [qemu64]
602	# qemu-system-riscv64 -machine andes_ae350 -cpu andes-ax46mpv ... -bios prog.elf
603	
604	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --dry-run --engine vsim:<cfg> prog.elf
605	# [andesim] dry-run: 2 command(s), not executed
606	# # command 1/2: fast-leg [qemu64]
607	# qemu-system-riscv64 ... -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 ... -readconfig <tmp>/qemu.cfg
608	# # command 2/2: accurate-leg [vsim:<cfg>]
609	# sim_<cfg> prog.elf --resume-from-qemu <tmp>/state-0.bin --handoff-out ...
610	```
611	
612	Supported VLEN range: 128 to 1024 bits. The handoff state file reserves
613	128 bytes per vector register (`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX`); an engine whose
614	VLEN exceeds 1024 is refused with a clear error instead of silently
615	truncating the V registers. A standalone fast run defaults to the
616	vector-capable CPU `andes-ax46mpv` (rv64) / `andes-a46mpv` (rv32), so RVV
617	binaries run out of the box at the cpu model's built-in VLEN; andesim itself
618	passes no `vlen`. To pin an exact VLEN, add a `-cpu` through the passthrough
619	tail, e.g. `andesim run --mode fast app.elf -- -cpu andes-ax46mpv,vlen=256`
620	(the last `-cpu` wins).
621	
622	Where `--` args land depends on the mode. `fast`/`cycle` forward them to their
623	single engine (qemu / vsim). `hybrid` has **two** legs (a QEMU fast-forward and
624	a vsim measure leg) whose command lines the driver builds itself, so there is no
625	single "the engine" to forward to -- `hybrid` therefore **rejects** `-- args`
626	(rc=2) rather than silently dropping them or guessing a leg. For vsim options use
627	the dedicated flags (`--kanata`/`--objdump`); to pin VLEN, pick the right
628	`--engine` (each vsim engine has a fixed VLEN).
629	
630	**`cycle` output.** A `cycle` run prints just two things: the program's own
631	output, then the cycle count as andesim's own one-line result --
632	
633	```
634	$ ./andesim run --mode cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium hello.elf
635	hello
636	[andesim] 3573 cycles
637	```
638	
639	vsim's startup banner (the `Copyright ... / Version :` lines) and its verbose
640	`[info]` log are hidden so the result stands alone; real `[warn]`/`[error]`
641	diagnostics still pass through, and the engine exit code is propagated. (`fast`
642	is raw passthrough -- QEMU's output is shown verbatim, and QEMU prints no such
643	banner or cycle line. `cycle --gdb` is interactive and is not filtered.)
644	
645	**Window boundary semantics.** Markers are HINT NOPs: the window is the
646	span strictly between them. A pc boundary is real user code: the
647	instruction at `--pc-start` executes
648	INSIDE the measured window -- the fast leg stops just before it and vsim
649	resumes at it, so no instruction is lost across the handoff. The
650	instruction at `--pc-end` is where vsim drains. `--pc-start` and `--pc-end`
651	must resolve to **different** addresses (compared numerically, so `main` and
652	its literal `0x..` address count as equal): an equal pair is an empty ROI --
653	vsim would drain the instant it resumes -- and is rejected up front with rc=2.
654	
655	> **Writing a kernel for cycle measurement (marker/PC modes):** keep the measured
656	> kernel anchored inside the `slti x0,x0,0x5A0/1` span -- read its inputs and
657	> write its outputs through memory inside the span, or wrap the kernel in a
658	> `__attribute__((noinline))` function called between the markers. The
659	> markers' `"memory"` clobber pins memory I/O but not register-only compute,
660	> so a kernel that carries live vector values in registers across the
661	> boundary may be hoisted/sunk out of the measured window. See
662	> `tests/fixtures/runtime/rt_c_helpers.h`.

677	
678	Quick env check:
679	
680	```sh
681	echo "$VSIM_QEMU"
682	echo "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
683	echo "$VSIM_BIN"
684	ls tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf
685	```
686	
687	### 4.1 marker mode - the default (kernel)
688	
689	Goal: run a vector fixture through QEMU1 -> vsim using the
690	two ROI markers (`slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1`) that the fixture already contains.
691	
692	```sh
693	./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium
694	```
695	
696	Expected output (stderr + stdout):
697	
698	```
699	[andesim] model=hybrid engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium vlen=<N> trigger=marker fixture=rt_c_v_matmul
700	[marker window_cycles] <N>  (vsim mcycle=<V> - qemu mcycle=<Q>)
701	PASS: --mode hybrid --trigger marker (rt_c_v_matmul)
702	```
703	
704	The relayed output is just the program's own prints plus andesim's own lines:
705	vsim's startup banner (the `Copyright ... / Version :` lines) is stripped from
706	the vsim leg, the same as `cycle` mode, so the result stands alone. (vsim's
707	`[info]` log never reaches here -- the leg's stderr is dropped at capture.)
708	
709	`./andesim run` orchestrates the two legs directly (no Python wrapper). Inside, the two legs are:
710	
711	```
712	1) QEMU1 with -plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=$STATE
713	        -> drain at slti x0,x0,0x5A0   -> exit 200
714	2) sim_ax45mpv_premium $ELF \
715	        --resume-from-qemu $STATE --handoff-out $STATE_V \
716	        --shared-mem-path $SHM --shared-mem-size 128MB
717	        -> ROI runs in vsim, drains at slti x0,x0,0x5A1   -> exit 200
718	```
719	
720	Try a different fixture:
721	
722	```sh
723	./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_matmul.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium
724	```
725	
726	### 4.2 PC mode - markerless workload, explicit boundary PCs
727	
728	Same plumbing as marker mode, but the binary carries **no** trigger markers.
729	The user picks the switch PCs explicitly via `--pc-start` and `--pc-end`,
730	each a symbol name or `0x` address. Both args are required for `--mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium`.
731	
732	Don't know where the hot region is? `build/hotloops` runs the binary
733	fast and reports the hottest loops (function, source line, PC range) as
734	an LLM-ready Markdown fact sheet. It auto-detects the QEMU binary,
735	plugin, and CPU from your build. Each loop block carries a `measure:`
736	field — a ready `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` pair that covers the enclosing
737	function entry to `ret` — that pastes straight into the command above.
738	`docs/andes_sim_gemm_tutorial.ipynb` walks that workflow end to end.
739	
740	```sh
741	./build/hotloops --min-iters 10 my_kernel.elf
742	```
743	
744	```sh
745	# resolve the boundary PCs once (cheap, host-side; needs HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
746	ELF=tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf
747	START=vmatmul_kernel
748	END=$(${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN}/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump -d "$ELF" \
749	        | awk '/<main>:/{flag=1} flag&&/jal[[:space:]]+.*<vmatmul_kernel>/{getline; print "0x"$1; exit}' \
750	        | tr -d ':')
751	
752	./andesim run "$ELF" --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --pc-start "$START" --pc-end "$END"
753	```
754	
755	`rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf` is the **markerless twin** of the GEMM fixture,
756	built `-DHYBRID_MARKERLESS` from the same source as the marked
757	`rt_c_v_matmul`. Both triggers are one-shot (QEMU plugin `exit(200)` on
758	first match; vsim drains on first match), so the measured window is
759	**exactly one full `vmatmul_kernel` call** (16 outer rows + inner k-loop
760	+ vse32 stores). The cycle count should land near marker mode's ~22808.
761	
762	The mechanism is fully general - pc mode can target **any** symbol or raw
763	address. `./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium` resolves `--pc-start` / `--pc-end` directly (symbol name or `0x` address) without needing env vars.
764	
765	The underlying QEMU and vsim invocations (what the driver orchestrates):
766	
767	```sh
768	# Resolve the boundaries (objdump-based; pick any two PCs in the ELF):
769	OBJDUMP=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump
770	NM=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm
771	ROI_START=$("$NM" tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
772	              | awk '$3=="vmatmul_kernel"{print "0x"$1}')
773	ROI_END=$("$OBJDUMP" -d tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
774	              | awk '/<main>:/{flag=1} flag&&/jal[[:space:]]+.*<vmatmul_kernel>/{getline; print "0x"$1; exit}' \
775	              | tr -d ':')
776	echo "enter=$ROI_START  exit=$ROI_END"   # e.g. 0x10021c / 0x1002cc
777	
778	# QEMU1 leg
779	"$VSIM_QEMU" \
780	  -object memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=/dev/shm/share,size=134217728 \
781	  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
782	  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
783	  -nographic \
784	  -bios tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
785	  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=/tmp/q1.bin,enter_pc=$ROI_START"
786	
787	# vsim leg
788	"$VSIM_BIN" tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
789	  --resume-from-qemu /tmp/q1.bin \
790	  --handoff-out /tmp/v.bin \
791	  --shared-mem-path /dev/shm/share \
792	  --shared-mem-size 134217728 \
793	  --hybrid-exit-pc "$ROI_END"
794	```
795	
796	The fixture binary differs from marker mode (markerless vs marked), and the
797	QEMU1 plugin and vsim flags carry hex PCs (`enter_pc=` / `--hybrid-exit-pc`)
798	instead of marker-trigger plumbing.
799	
800	### 4.3 Capturing a Kanata pipeline trace of the ROI
801	
802	When debugging a hot path on vsim, pass `--kanata FILE` to `./andesim run`
803	in marker or pc mode. The resulting trace contains pipeline records only
804	for the ROI region (between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain) -- vsim
805	boot and DMI resume overhead are filtered out.
806	
807	```sh
808	# marker mode: the ROI is the span between the two ROI markers (slti x0,x0,0x5A0/1)
809	# markers already in the source. vsim auto-derives the window.
810	./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf \
811	  --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata
812	
813	# pc mode: the ROI bounds are whatever PCs you passed.
814	./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
815	  --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x1002cc \
816	  --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata
817	```
818	
819	Add `--objdump FILE` so the kanata `L` records embed the disassembly
820	text next to each PC. Generate the dump once with the toolchain
821	`objdump -d`:
822	
823	```sh
824	$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump -d \
825	  tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf > /tmp/roi.S
826	./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf \
827	  --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata --objdump /tmp/roi.S
828	```
829	
830	Open `/tmp/roi.kanata` in [Konata](https://github.com/shioyadan/Konata)
831	to view the pipeline.
832	
833	Constraints:
834	
835	- `--kanata` is only valid with `--mode hybrid --trigger marker` or `--mode hybrid --trigger pc` (the only triggers with a single ROI-exit PC); any other trigger is rejected with rc=2.
836	- marker mode requires exactly one `slti x0,x0,0x5A1` (exit marker) in the
837	  ELF. If the binary has more than one, vsim errors out with
838	  `multiple ... markers in ELF -- use \`--mode hybrid --trigger pc\` with explicit \`--pc-end\``.
839	  Switch to pc mode and pick the desired exit explicitly.
840	- `--objdump` requires `--kanata`.
841	
842	How it works:
843	
844	- `./andesim` appends `--kanata FILE --kanata-roi`
845	  (and `--objdump FILE`) to vsim's argv.
846	- vsim's `--kanata-roi` flag defers the kanata enable until after
847	  `--resume-from-qemu` loads the input state and `enable_hybrid_handoff`
848	  scans the ELF, then derives a one-shot `LoopGate`:
849	  - `start_pc` = the resumed PC (where vsim first fetches user code)
850	  - `end_pc`   = `--hybrid-exit-pc` (pc mode) or the unique
851	    `slti x0,x0,0x5A1` PC from CsrTrigger (marker mode)
852	  - `skip_iters=0`, `record_iters=1` (open on first fetch of start_pc,
853	    close on first retire of end_pc).
854	
855	### 4.4 Verifying a hybrid run against a QEMU oracle (`--verify`)
856	
857	With the QEMU2 handback removed, the code after your ROI never runs, so a
858	hybrid run normally proves only that a cycle figure came out. `--verify`
859	(default OFF) cross-checks the run's correctness:
860	
861	```sh
862	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --verify your_prog.elf
863	# ...
864	# [marker window_cycles] 46  (vsim mcycle=... - qemu mcycle=...)
865	# [state-diff] PASS: 109 fields match (counters and passthrough CSRs excluded)
866	# [verify] PASS: vsim drain matches the QEMU oracle
867	```
868	
869	Performance note: without `--verify`, the vsim leg drains only `mcycle`/`minstret`
870	(the cycle figure) and skips reading back the full architectural register file
871	over the Debug Module. A full drain reads every GPR, FPR, and transported CSR
872	with one Abstract Command each (only the vector registers ride a Program-Buffer
873	sweep through the shared scratch page); those simulated debug cycles dominate
874	hybrid wall-clock for a short ROI but never affect the cycle count -- the
875	counters are read before the rest of the drain. `--verify` needs every field
876	for the diff, so it keeps the full drain; expect a `--verify` run to take
877	noticeably longer than the same run without it.
878	
879	How it works: after the normal run, the same ELF re-runs on pure QEMU (the
880	oracle) with the plugin draining at the ROI exit boundary, sampled at the
881	exact pc where vsim halted. The pre-ROI path is QEMU in both runs, so the
882	ROI inputs are identical -- any architectural divergence inside the ROI
883	(RTL bug, state-restore bug, drain bug) shows up as a field mismatch and
884	the run exits non-zero, listing each differing field:
885	
886	```
887	[state-diff] x10: ref=0x3d got=0x0
888	[state-diff] FAIL: 1 mismatch(es) (115 fields compared)
889	```
890	
891	What is compared: pc, all GPRs, all FPRs (when FP state is live), the V
892	CSRs and full vector registers (when V state is live), and the writable
893	M-mode CSRs that round-trip through the handoff -- `mscratch` (L23) and
894	`mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie` (L24), restored at resume and re-read at
895	drain. What is not:
896	
897	- `mcycle`/`minstret` -- the engines count differently by design;
898	- `mip` -- restored and re-read, but its pending bits are hardware-driven
899	  (the timer bit tracks elapsed time, which differs between QEMU's
900	  functional clock and vsim's cycle clock), so a compare would
901	  false-positive;
902	- `mstatus`, `mtvec` -- passthrough: vsim restores the QEMU1 entry snapshot value; both sides hold the same bits by construction so comparing is trivially true but not useful;
903	- `satp`, `medeleg`/`mideleg` -- S-mode CSRs, not implemented on the default M-only engine. The privilege level itself IS compared: both
904	  sides drain the real one (L6), so a wrong-privilege resume shows up as
905	  a priv mismatch.
906	
907	The handoff also carries the **v6 write-mask**: the plugin tracks which config
908	CSRs (the Andes block, PMA, the M-ext block, `mcache_ctl`/`mmisc_ctl`) your
909	program actually WROTE, and the cycle engine restores -- and `--verify`
910	compares -- only those. A CSR the program never touched keeps the engine's own
911	reset value instead of inheriting QEMU's reset default, so reset-value
912	differences between QEMU and any engine cannot skew the run. The tracking is
913	translation-time work in the plugin (only CSR-write instructions get a
914	callback), so the fast leg's speed is unaffected.
915	
916	The write-mask also powers an **incompatibility warning** on every hybrid run
917	(not just `--verify`): if your program wrote a config CSR the chosen cycle
918	engine does not implement, the driver prints
919	
920	```
921	[andesim] warning: the program wrote CSRs engine vsim:<engine> does not
922	implement: <names> (on this engine's silicon these writes would trap; the
923	hybrid restore skipped them)
924	```
925	
926	to stderr. On that engine's real silicon the `csrw` would trap before the ROI,
927	so the cycle figure may not represent this program on this engine -- pick an
928	engine that implements those CSRs, or drop the writes. A clean run prints
929	nothing.
930	
931	The handoff also carries the **v5 L2C block**: the L2 cache controller's MMIO
932	register window (0x0000..0x0527, base 0xE0500000). This is device MMIO, not a
933	CSR -- the QEMU plugin reads the window by physical address, and vsim writes back
934	only the writable boot-static config registers (Control 0x0008 = `CEN` enable +
935	prefetch + ECC + RAM timing, HPM Control, Way Allocation Masks) via
936	Program-Buffer stores before resuming. It is the L2 analog of the L1 `mcache_ctl`
937	transport and matters for the cycle figure the same way: an L2-enabled engine
938	that resumed with L2 disabled would run the ROI severalfold slower. Restore is
939	gated on the cycle engine actually having an L2C (`NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB > 0`);
940	every engine shipped today is built without one, so the block rides
941	forward-looking and no-ops. `--verify` compares the Control Register (masking the
942	read-only INITSTATUS bit).
943	
944	The handoff also carries the v3 Andes block (`mxstatus`, ILM/DLM bases, PMA, ...)
945	and the **v4 M-ext block** (`HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST`): the writable M-mode CSRs
946	across the whole AndeStar V5 SPA -- perf counters, NMI, CLIC, trap-save,
947	state-enable, debug triggers, ePMP, CCTL, peripheral bases, U-mode Andes control
948	(51 CSRs). Every one is **capability-gated by CSR address**: an engine restores,
949	drains, and `--verify`-compares only the CSRs its config implements (reported via
950	`--describe andes_csrs`), so a CSR the core lacks is a no-op rather than a DM
951	hang. On the default `ax45mpv_premium` (M-only) that gates on the perf-monitor +
952	trigger CSRs; the rest ride forward-looking for a CLIC / Smrnmi / Smstateen /
953	M+U-capable engine. A few supported-but-engine-divergent CSRs are transported and
954	restored but excluded from `--verify` (like `msp_bound`): the HW perf counters
955	`mhpmcounter3-6`, `mdcause`, the trigger defaults `tdata1`/`tcontrol`, and the
956	ILM/DLM base+enable CSRs `milmb`/`mdlmb` (their enable bit reads 1 on the vsim
957	RTL but 0 on QEMU, which models no local memory). The
958	complete per-CSR disposition for all 232 spec CSRs is in
959	`docs/csr_coverage.ipynb`, guarded against drift by
960	`tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py`.
961	
962	Per-engine CSR validation is a registration requirement: every supported
963	engine build carries its own CSR manifest + registration report under
964	`tests/engines/` (contract: `tests/engines/README.md`). For a human-readable
965	answer to "which CSRs does this engine restore, and under which condition --
966	or why not", read the engine's `csr_restore_table.md` in the same directory
967	(generated from the manifest by `tests/engines/render_restore_table.py`;
968	`test_restore_table.sh` guards it against drift).
969	`docs/engine_registration_tutorial.ipynb` walks the whole lifecycle --
970	the three-way audit (spec x config.inc x RTL), registering a new engine or
971	config, and removing one. `docs/csr_transport_bringup_tutorial.ipynb` is the
972	companion reference: what the `/csr-transport-bringup` skill does (its 7-phase
973	pipeline), every column of `csr_manifest.csv`, and each file a registration
974	ships under `tests/engines/<engine>-<confighash>/`.
975	
976	Costs and limits: the oracle leg is one extra QEMU run of the whole
977	program (MHz-class -- cheap next to the vsim leg). `--verify` works with
978	`--trigger marker|pc`, assumes the single-shot ROI the hybrid run itself
979	assumes, and requires `--mode hybrid` (the other models have nothing to
980	cross-check).

# Hybrid Simulator User Guide

Audience: a new engineer who wants to RUN the Andes hybrid simulator,
not study its internals. After this guide you can:

1. Build every artifact from a fresh clone.
2. Configure QEMU, vsim, and the driver for a workload.
3. Pick a switching mode (marker or PC) and run one handoff end-to-end
   with a concrete worked example.

For per-mode drill-down, read `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md`.

---

## 0. The one-paragraph mental model

QEMU runs the boring parts at MHz. vsim (Verilator + SystemC) runs the
small region-of-interest at cycle accuracy. They share RAM via an
`mmap` file. A magic trigger (marker HINT or PC)
hands control between them. One run is two legs:

```
   QEMU1  -- state.bin + shared mmap -->  vsim
   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)
```

The thing you choose per run is the TRIGGER that decides where each
leg drains and the next leg resumes. That choice is the "switching
mode".

---

## 0.5 Quick start with `./andesim`

`./andesim` is the canonical end-user entry point (the C++ driver; it
self-builds on first use). It drives `run` itself, orchestrating QEMU and
vsim directly; building is done by `scripts/build_all.sh` (which delegates to
`setup.sh`, `scripts/build_*.sh`). Sections 1-7 document those underlying
scripts (`tests/e2e.sh`, `scripts/run_e2e.sh`) for when you need to bypass
the driver.

Four-command worked example - cold checkout to passing suite:

```sh
bash scripts/build_all.sh                             # qemu, vsim, plugin, fixtures
./andesim list engines                                # discover the built engines
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf                         # one marker-mode handoff
JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh                          # the hybrid e2e suite (or scripts/test_all.sh for unit+contract+e2e)
```

Expected last line of `scripts/run_e2e.sh`:

```
summary: marker <N>p/0f/<S>s  pc <N>p/0f/<S>s  neg <N>p/0f/0s  total <N> passed, 0 failed, <S> skipped
```

Subcommand cheat sheet:

| Command                                                          | What it does                                                        |
|------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `./andesim list <models|engines>`                              | List the 3 models, or the discovered engines with their hardware params (XLEN/VLEN/DLEN/ELEN; `-` = not reported). |
| `bash scripts/build_all.sh [TARGET] [--dry-run]`               | Build artifacts; targets: `all`, `plugin`, `fixtures`, `runtime` (qemu and vsim are external prebuilt binaries, not built here). |
| `./andesim doctor`                                             | Read-only environment health check: artifacts, submodules, toolchain, runtime, discovered engines, and `/dev/shm` mmap tiers (with WSL2 advice). |
| `./andesim run --mode fast|cycle|hybrid [--trigger marker|pc] [--engine ID] [--gdb [--gdb-port PORT]] <elf>` | Run one ELF on a model (hybrid = QEMU -> vsim handoff and REQUIRES `--trigger marker|pc` to delimit the ROI; --gdb pauses at startup for a debugger: fast opens QEMU's GDB stub on port 1234, cycle halts the hart and opens vsim's JTAG port (9104) then execs `$ICEMAN`, a GDB server (use a modern OpenOCD); --gdb not supported with hybrid). |
| `bash scripts/run_e2e.sh` (env: `FILTER`, `MODE`, `JOBS`)        | Run the hybrid e2e suite directly (qemu+vsim round-trips). |
| `bash scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit\|contract\|e2e]`     | Run the full test surface: C++ unit tests + driver contracts + the e2e suite. |

Run `./andesim <cmd> -h` for the full flag list of a subcommand (set
`ANDESIM_DEV=1` to reveal developer-only flags and the `list fixtures`
target). The rest of this guide (Sections 1-7) documents the
underlying scripts and is useful when you need to bypass `./andesim`
(custom env vars, single-leg debugging, alternative CPU YAML, etc.).

---

## 1. Build and environment setup

### 1.1 Host prerequisites

Install these on the host once:

| Package          | Notes                                                |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `git`            | clone the repo and its submodules                    |
| C/C++ toolchain  | clang or gcc; needed by QEMU and the plugin          |
| `cmake` >= 3.20  | vsim build                                           |
| `ninja`          | vsim default generator                               |
| `python3`        | plugin tests, engine deriver scripts                 |
| `glib-2.0` dev   | QEMU plugin link line                                |
| `pkg-config`     | plugin build (glib-2.0)                              |
| `podman`         | runs vsim builds inside `vsim-env:latest` container  |
| Verilator        | auto-detected; set `VSIM_VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE` if needed |
| QEMU             | prebuilt external binary; set `QEMU_BIN_DIR` (not built here) |
| RISC-V toolchain | `riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,nm,objdump}` (Andes v5d)   |

The Andes RISC-V toolchain is needed to build the fixtures and to
resolve symbols for PC-mode. The harness scripts default to
`/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/.../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`;
override with `NM=/your/path/to/nm` if you keep it elsewhere.

### 1.2 Clone with submodules

```sh
git clone --recursive https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim
cd hybrid_sim
```

If you forgot `--recursive`:

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

Submodules under this repo:

| Path             | What it is                                          |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| `include/`     | the shared ABI (`andesim_abi` repo): `hybrid_state_v1` wire contract under `include/hybrid/` |

vsim is no longer a submodule -- it is a prebuilt **external** binary, like QEMU.
Build it in your own vsim (`hybrid_vsim`) checkout and point `VSIM_BIN_DIR`
(`config.env`) at its `build/` dir; see 1.3.

### 1.3 Per-host config (`config.env`)

The repo ships a template `config.env.example` listing per-host paths
that cannot live in the build system (notably the Andes RISC-V
toolchain root, which `setup.sh` does NOT build).

On the first `source ./setup.sh`, the template is copied to
`./config.env` (gitignored) so your edits never touch git history. If
the toolchain lives somewhere other than the default, edit
`config.env`:

```sh
# config.env
HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d
HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds32le-elf-newlib-v5d
```

The variables today:

| Variable            | What it points at                                                  |
|---------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN`  | rv64 toolchain root. `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/` must contain `riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,ld,nm,objdump,...}`. |
| `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32`| rv32 toolchain root (a *separate* install), for building the rv32 runtime + fixtures. `bin/` must contain `riscv32-unknown-elf-{gcc,ar,...}`. Optional: leave unset if you only target rv64 (rv32 builds are skipped). |
| `QEMU_BIN_DIR`      | External prebuilt QEMU build dir holding `qemu-system-riscv64` AND `qemu-system-riscv32` (this repo no longer builds QEMU). |
| `VSIM_BIN_DIR`      | External prebuilt vsim build dir holding the `sim_*` binaries (this repo no longer builds vsim; the driver discovers cycle engines by scanning it). |

How it propagates:

  exists, and `export`s the variable so all child processes see it.

- The unified `e2e.sh` test harness loads `config.env` itself when run
  without prior `source ./setup.sh`, then derives

## 2. Configuring the simulator

There are four configuration surfaces. Most users only touch the env
vars in 2.1.

### 2.1 Environment variables (the only ones you usually set)

`setup.sh` exports these for you. Override only if your artifacts live
somewhere non-default.

| Variable        | Default                                          | Used by                  |
|-----------------|--------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|
| `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` | From `config.env` (sec 1.3); toolchain root  | Makefile, NM derivation  |
| `VSIM_QEMU`     | `$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64` (external)    | every harness            |
| `VSIM_PLUGIN`   | `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`               | every harness            |
| `VSIM_BIN`      | first `$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_*`                     | every harness            |
| `VSIM_ELF`      | `tests/fixtures/$FIXTURE.elf`           | harness scripts          |
| `NM`            | `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`   | PC-mode symbol resolve   |
| `TIMEOUT`       | 60 s (120 for long runs)                         | per-leg `timeout` cap    |
| `FIXTURE`       | `rt_shared_mem`                                  | which `.elf` to load     |
| `TRIGGER_MODE`  | `marker`                                            | `marker` or `pc`            |
| `JOBS`          | auto-cap on this 128-core host: set to 8         | parallel test runner     |
| `HSIM_MMAP_DIR` | tier list (`/dev/shm`, then `~/.cache/andesim`) | pin one backing dir for `--mem-size` (disables the fallback) |

Example: override the QEMU binary for one run:

```sh
VSIM_QEMU=/opt/qemu-9.0/qemu-system-riscv64 \
  ./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium
```

### 2.2 The vsim CPU configuration YAML

vsim is built in its own external checkout (the `hybrid_vsim` repo, pointed at by
`VSIM_BIN_DIR`); the commands in this section run THERE, not in andesim. Its
`config.yaml` selects which Andes core to verilate. The default is
`ax45mpv_premium`:

```yaml
cpus:
  ax45mpv_premium:
    cpu_series: 45
    rtl_package: ax45mpv_premium
    cpp_wrapper: ax45mpv_premium_cpu_cluster_subsystem
    config: data/configs/ax45mpv_premium.cfg
    config_dir: andes_ip/kv_core/top/hdl
    config_inc_filter: grep '^`define NDS_'
    extra_verilator_flags: --threads 8 --unroll-count 256
```

Switch CPU by pointing CMake at a different YAML (in your vsim checkout):

```sh
cd <your vsim checkout>   # e.g. /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DVSIM_CONFIG_FILE=my_other_cpu.yaml
cmake --build build -j
```

`-DVSIM_NO_VERILATOR=ON` skips Verilator (use a prebuilt model). The
hybrid doctest unit tests are always registered with CTest (run via
`ctest` or the `check` target).

### 2.3 QEMU plugin args

The plugin reads `arg=value` tokens after `-plugin <path>,`. They
select WHICH switching mode QEMU1 runs in:

| Plugin arg           | Effect                                                                 |
|----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `outfile=PATH`       | REQUIRED. Drained `hybrid_state_v1` is written here.                   |
| `enter_pc=0xADDR`    | PC mode: drain when PC == ADDR. Bypasses the marker-insn matcher.         |
| `exit_marker=1`      | Oracle exit drain (verification): arm on the EXIT marker `slti x0,x0,0x5A1`, drain right after it retires. The run never hands off -- it produces the reference state `--verify` compares against. Exclusive with the other mode args. |
| `exit_pc=0xADDR`     | Oracle exit drain, pc form: arm when PC == ADDR instead of on the exit marker. |
| `drain_pc=0xADDR`    | Oracle modifier: after arming, drain at the first hit of ADDR (the verifier passes vsim's drained pc here, so both sides sample the same architectural point -- vsim's DMI halt lands a few insns past the trigger). |
| `ilm_size=BYTES`, `dlm_size=BYTES` | LM content transport: additionally drain that many bytes of ILM/DLM content (read through the hart-0 local-memory slave ports) into raw sidecar files `<outfile>.ilm` / `<outfile>.dlm`. Default 0 = skip (engine without that local memory); the driver passes the paired engine's sizes. |
| `ilm_base=0xADDR`, `dlm_base=0xADDR` | Override the LM slave-port bases (defaults `0xA0000000` / `0xA0200000`, AE350 hart 0). |
| `hvm_size=BYTES`     | HVM content transport: drain that many bytes of the High-Bandwidth Vector Memory into `<outfile>.hvm`, same contract as the LM sidecars. Default 0 = skip. |
| `hvm_base=0xADDR`    | Override the HVM subordinate-port base (default `0x90000000`, AE350). |

If no mode arg is given, the default is marker-insn match (marker mode): the
plugin matches `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` at retire.

Example invocation (marker mode, just the minimal arg):

```
-plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=/tmp/state.bin
```

### 2.4 vsim CLI flags

`sim_ax45mpv_premium <elf> [flags]`. The hybrid-relevant subset:

| Flag                          | Purpose                                                  |
|-------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| `--resume-from-qemu FILE`     | Read drained state, restore into hart, run from PC.     |
| `--handoff-out FILE`          | Drain back into FILE when the exit trigger fires.       |
| `--shared-mem-path FILE`      | mmap FILE as RAM (zero-copy share with QEMU).           |
| `--shared-mem-size BYTES`     | Size of the shared region. Match QEMU `-m`.             |
| `--shared-mem-base HEX`       | Guest physical address where file offset 0 lands.       |
| `--hybrid-exit-pc 0xADDR`     | PC mode exit: drain when this PC retires.               |
| `--drain-minimal`             | Exit drain reads back only mcycle/minstret; the driver sets it when `--verify` is off. |
| `--no-reset-baseline`         | Disable the liveness gate (below): restore every transported register. |
| `--jtag-port N`               | Open the JTAG bitbang port (ICEman or OpenOCD). The hart free-runs; the debugger halts it over the JTAG DTM on connect. The `./andesim run --mode cycle --gdb` path opens this port for ICEman (set `$ICEMAN`). |
| `--log-level N`               | 0=trace .. 5=critical .. 6=off (default 2=info)         |

`--shared-mem-base` must be the guest physical address of RAM: `0x0` on the
`andes_ae350` machine (its DRAM window is `0x0..0x7fffffff`; `0x80000000` is
the boot MROM, and vsim's built-in `0x80000000` default targets the upstream
`virt` machine). The driver always passes `0x0`; only standalone vsim
invocations need to override it.

**Liveness gate (reset baseline).** Every register moved through the Debug
Module costs hundreds of simulated cycles, and most transported state still
holds its reset value. So the resume skips any restore whose drained value
equals the engine's own reset value -- a no-op write. The very first hybrid
run of a given (engine build, ELF) pair drains that reset state once (a few
extra seconds) and caches it under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/` (fallback
`~/.cache/andesim/`); later runs load the cache and typically cut the vsim
leg by ~4x (hello: 50k -> 12k simulated cycles). The cache self-invalidates
on engine rebuild or ELF change (mtime+size keyed); delete the directory to
force a fresh capture. `--verify` works unchanged with the gate active;
`--no-reset-baseline` restores the old transport-everything behavior.

Run `$VSIM_BIN --help` for the full list (waveform/save/restore are
license-gated and off by default).

### 2.5 Requesting memory (`--mem-size` + `HSIM_MMAP_DIR`)

By default every `./andesim` invocation that needs a shared mmap allocates
a 128 MiB sparse file under `/dev/shm` (tmpfs, RAM-backed). When your
workload's memory footprint exceeds `/dev/shm` capacity (typically
RAM/2 on Linux), two knobs let you redirect:

| Knob              | Where             | What it does |
|-------------------|-------------------|--------------|
| `--mem-size SPEC` | flag on `run` (`--mmap-size` is the old alias) | request guest program memory (`SPEC` = `128M`, `1.5G`, `2G`, or raw bytes). Cap `2G` minus one 4 KiB V-transport page (the AE350 DRAM window). |
| `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/path` | env var | pin the backing directory (skips the tier list below). |

Per-model semantics of `--mem-size`:

| Model    | What it does |
|----------|--------------|
| `hybrid` | `--mem-size` is your **program** RAM (default `128M`). The driver maps one extra 4 KiB page on top for the V-register transport scratch (L26): the physical shared mmap = QEMU memory backend = vsim RAM window = `--mem-size + 4 KiB`, with the scratch parked in that top page, just above everything your program can address. You get your full `--mem-size`; the page is invisible. The driver rejects `> 2G - 4 KiB` **before** allocating, and rejects an ELF whose static image would extend into the reserved page (`raise --mem-size`). |
| `fast`   | forwards a plain QEMU `-m`. Without the flag the argv is untouched -- QEMU as-is, its own 128 MiB default, no mmap involved. No `2G` cap here (that ceiling is the hybrid shared-mmap window, not fast's); QEMU itself validates the size and rejects only oversized values (`Cannot model more than 16GB RAM` on the AE350 machine). |
| `cycle`  | validate-only: the cycle engine always models its full DRAM window, so there is nothing to size (the driver says so on stderr). |

Backing-directory selection (`./andesim`): a two-tier list, first fit
wins (fit = size + 256 MiB free):

1. `/dev/shm` -- tmpfs, RAM speed. Skipped when absent or too small.
2. `~/.cache/andesim` (honors `XDG_CACHE_HOME`) -- disk-backed; the
   size ceiling becomes disk free space. Hot pages still sit in the
   kernel page cache, so the cost vs tmpfs is background writeback only.

We never switch **silently**: the status line always names the chosen
dir, and a fallback adds the reason, e.g.
`[hsim mmap] 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andesim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))`.
`HSIM_MMAP_DIR` pins a single dir with **no** fallback past it: rc=2
with a hint if it can't hold the request.

Examples:

```sh
# Small request; /dev/shm fits, so tier 1 is chosen.
./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 256M
#   [hsim mmap] 256.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 252.0 GiB)

# Near-max request on a small-RAM box: falls through to the disk tier,
# and the status line says so. (2047M is the hybrid ceiling -- exactly 2G is
# rejected because the extra V-scratch page would overflow the DRAM window.)
./andesim run my.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 2047M
#   [hsim mmap] 2.0 GiB at /home/u/.cache/andesim (free: 2.1 TiB) (fallback: /dev/shm too small (1.2 GiB free))

# Pin a scratch filesystem instead (no fallback past the pin):
HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/scratch \
  ./andesim run my.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 2047M
```

If you pin `HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/tmp` and `/tmp` is mounted as tmpfs (Arch
default), that does not lift the RAM ceiling; pick a directory on a
non-tmpfs filesystem (`/var/tmp`, `/scratch`, etc.) -- or just let the
tier list pick `~/.cache/andesim` for you.

The hardcoded `mktemp -p /dev/shm` paths in the shell harnesses
(`tests/e2e.sh`, `tests/drivers/*.sh`, `tests/plugin/*.sh`) all use
128 MiB and are unaffected.

### 2.5.1 Running on WSL2 and macOS

The hybrid handoff needs both legs (QEMU and vsim) on **one Linux
kernel**, with the mmap file on a filesystem local to that kernel.
That rule decides what each OS needs:

**Linux** -- native, nothing to do.

**Windows (WSL2)** -- works as Linux; two caveats:

- Keep the repo and the mmap dirs on the ext4 side (`~/...`), never
  under `/mnt/c` (drvfs is slow and `MAP_SHARED` is not coherent there).
- `/dev/shm` is capped by the WSL VM memory. Raise `memory=` in
  `%UserProfile%\.wslconfig` if tier 1 is too small -- or just let the
  tier list fall through to `~/.cache/andesim`.

`./andesim doctor` checks both (see the `mmap tiers:` section and the
WSL warnings at the end of its report).

**macOS** -- run-only. vsim is a Linux binary, so `./andesim` re-execs
the run inside a prebuilt Linux runtime image in the podman machine VM;
the mmap lives inside that VM (the container's `/dev/shm`), never on a
virtiofs mount. One-time setup:

```sh
brew install podman
podman machine init --memory 4096   # the VM hosts /dev/shm (tier 1)
podman machine start
podman pull <runtime image>         # or load a CI-built andesim-runtime:latest
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --mem-size 256M my.elf
```

Knobs: `ANDESIM_IMAGE` (image name, default `andesim-runtime:latest`),
`ANDESIM_SHM_SIZE` (container `/dev/shm`, default `3g`),
`ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE` (podman/docker). Your current directory is
bind-mounted at the same path, so relative ELF paths and output files
work; builds (`scripts/build_all.sh`) stay Linux-only. The image is built on
Linux from `Dockerfile.runtime` (it bakes a fully built repo at
`/opt/hybrid_sim`); Apple Silicon runs the x86-64 image under emulation,
so expect slower wall-clock than a Linux host.

### 2.6 The hybrid guest memory map (`--print-memmap`)

Which addresses may a hybrid workload touch? Print the map for exactly the
run you are about to do (same `--engine` / `--mem-size`; the ELF is optional
and only adds a fit note):

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --mem-size 128M
```

```
REGION           BASE         END          SIZE    TRANSPORT
DRAM             0x0          0x7ffffff    128M    shared mmap; content survives the handoff
V-scratch        0x8000000    0x8000fff    4K      reserved by the hybrid V transport; not program-usable
ILM              0x0          0xffff       64K     sidecar .ilm; DRAM overlay while milmb.IEN=1
DLM              0x200000     0x207fff     32K     sidecar .dlm; DRAM overlay while mdlmb.IEN=1
HVM              0x90000000   0x9003ffff   256K    sidecar .hvm
SimControl/HTIF  0xe0080000   0xe0080fff   4K      device; state does not cross the handoff
UART2            0xf0300000   0xf03fffff   1M      device (console); state does not cross the handoff
```

Reading the table:

- **END is the inclusive last byte**; SIZE is the region span.
- **DRAM** tracks `--mem-size`; the **V-scratch** page above it belongs to
  the V-register transport (2.5) -- the driver rejects an ELF that reaches
  into it.
- **ILM/DLM/HVM** rows appear only when the engine can actually transport
  their content (`--describe` sizes > 0, the backdoor gate); their bases come
  from the engine's own `--print-qemu-config` geometry -- the same file the
  QEMU leg boots with -- so the printed map IS the run's effective one.
- **Devices**: only the vplat set both engines model is listed. Device STATE
  never crosses the handoff (each engine has its own UART/SimControl
  instance); only RAM content does.
- Anything NOT in the table is unsupported in hybrid mode: it is modeled by
  one engine only (QEMU's PLIC/PLMT/MROM/virtio..., vsim's debug-module
  window), so touching it inside the ROI gives engine-specific behavior.

The map is hybrid-only surface: `--mode fast|cycle` run one engine's native
map, which the driver does not model (`--print-memmap` errors there). vsim's
own `--print-memmap` dumps its interconnect routing table -- useful for
engine bring-up, but it is one engine's view, not the hybrid contract;
`tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_print_memmap.sh` cross-checks the two so they
cannot drift apart.
