## 3. Switching modes - which trigger to use

| Mode     | Profiles          | Switch boundary                                          | Cycle figure           |
|----------|-------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|------------------------|
| marker   | a kernel          | `slti x0,x0,0x5A0/1` insn match (markers in source)         | kernel cycles          |
| PC       | a kernel          | PC equals a boundary: any symbol or `0x` address (both `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` required) | kernel cycles |

Marker/PC delimit ONE kernel you choose. Both go through `./andesim run
--mode hybrid --trigger marker|pc`. The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle`
delta.

Decision flow:

```
Profiling ONE region you can name (a kernel)?
  binary is yours to edit          -> marker (andesim_ROI_begin()/end() around it)
  not editable, symbol/PC at ends  -> PC   (./andesim run --mode hybrid
                                            --trigger pc --pc-start S --pc-end E)
```

**Hardware-config sync.** A hybrid run models ONE core on two engines, so
the QEMU fast leg inherits the selected engine's hardware config. Three
things flow from engine to QEMU, all derived from the engine's frozen
`config.inc`:

- **VLEN** comes from the engine's `--describe` (512 when the engine
  reports none) and shows in the run banner as `vlen=N`.
- **The ISA** (extensions: CoDense, Zfh, Zba/Zbb/Zbc/Zbs, `xandesv5isa`,
  ...) comes from the engine's `--print-qemu-config`: the driver captures
  that QEMU `-readconfig` cfg and hands it to the fast leg, so QEMU executes
  the same extensions the engine models instead of a fixed `-cpu` string.
  An engine built without the flag (an older binary) makes the driver fall
  back to its default `-cpu` with no error. See `docs/qemu_match_ROADMAP.md`.
- **ILM/DLM content** (`--describe` `ilm_size`/`dlm_size`, bytes): when the
  engine has local memories, the fast leg's plugin also drains their content
  into `<state>.ilm`/`.dlm` sidecar files and the vsim leg loads them back
  (`--ilm`/`--dlm`), so a program that stages code/data in TCM before the ROI
  resumes with that content in place. An engine without local memories (or an
  older binary that does not report them) adds nothing. A guest that uses TCM
  must enable it itself (write `milmb`/`mdlmb`) -- which real TCM firmware
  does anyway; that CSR write rides the v6 write-mask so the enable is
  restored on the vsim leg. See `ROADMAP_ilm_dlm.md`.
- **HVM content** (`--describe` `hvm_size`, bytes): same contract for the
  High-Bandwidth Vector Memory at `0x90000000` -- the plugin drains
  `<state>.hvm`, the vsim leg backdoor-loads it (`--hvm`), and the exit
  drain dumps it back next to the handoff-out state. A program that stages
  vector data in HVM before the ROI resumes with that data in place; there
  is no enable bit (the geometry CSRs `mhvm_cfg`/`mhvmb` are read-only
  constants both sides derive from the same config). See `ROADMAP_hvm.md`.

An engine whose XLEN is not 64 (e.g. `vsim:d23`, rv32) cannot share
architectural state with the rv64 fast leg and is rejected with a clear
error.

**Preview the commands (`--dry-run`).** Add `--dry-run` to **any** mode
(`fast`, `cycle`, or `hybrid`) to print the exact engine command line(s) --
fully resolved and shell-quoted, including any matched `-readconfig` and all
paths -- and run nothing. `fast`/`cycle` print their single standalone command;
`hybrid` prints both legs:

```
./andesim run --mode fast --dry-run prog.elf
# [andesim] dry-run: 1 command(s), not executed
# # command 1/1: standalone [qemu64]
# qemu-system-riscv64 -machine andes_ae350 -cpu andes-ax46mpv ... -bios prog.elf

./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --dry-run --engine vsim:<cfg> prog.elf
# [andesim] dry-run: 2 command(s), not executed
# # command 1/2: fast-leg [qemu64]
# qemu-system-riscv64 ... -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 ... -readconfig <tmp>/qemu.cfg
# # command 2/2: accurate-leg [vsim:<cfg>]
# sim_<cfg> prog.elf --resume-from-qemu <tmp>/state-0.bin --handoff-out ...
```

Supported VLEN range: 128 to 1024 bits. The handoff state file reserves
128 bytes per vector register (`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX`); an engine whose
VLEN exceeds 1024 is refused with a clear error instead of silently
truncating the V registers. A standalone fast run defaults to the
vector-capable CPU `andes-ax46mpv` (rv64) / `andes-a46mpv` (rv32), so RVV
binaries run out of the box at the cpu model's built-in VLEN; andesim itself
passes no `vlen`. To pin an exact VLEN, add a `-cpu` through the passthrough
tail, e.g. `andesim run --mode fast app.elf -- -cpu andes-ax46mpv,vlen=256`
(the last `-cpu` wins).

Where `--` args land depends on the mode. `fast`/`cycle` forward them to their
single engine (qemu / vsim). `hybrid` has **two** legs (a QEMU fast-forward and
a vsim measure leg) whose command lines the driver builds itself, so there is no
single "the engine" to forward to -- `hybrid` therefore **rejects** `-- args`
(rc=2) rather than silently dropping them or guessing a leg. For vsim options use
the dedicated flags (`--kanata`/`--objdump`); to pin VLEN, pick the right
`--engine` (each vsim engine has a fixed VLEN).

**`cycle` output.** A `cycle` run prints just two things: the program's own
output, then the cycle count as andesim's own one-line result --

```
$ ./andesim run --mode cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium hello.elf
hello
[andesim] 3573 cycles
```

vsim's startup banner (the `Copyright ... / Version :` lines) and its verbose
`[info]` log are hidden so the result stands alone; real `[warn]`/`[error]`
diagnostics still pass through, and the engine exit code is propagated. (`fast`
is raw passthrough -- QEMU's output is shown verbatim, and QEMU prints no such
banner or cycle line. `cycle --gdb` is interactive and is not filtered.)

**Window boundary semantics.** Markers are HINT NOPs: the window is the
span strictly between them. A pc boundary is real user code: the
instruction at `--pc-start` executes
INSIDE the measured window -- the fast leg stops just before it and vsim
resumes at it, so no instruction is lost across the handoff. The
instruction at `--pc-end` is where vsim drains. `--pc-start` and `--pc-end`
must resolve to **different** addresses (compared numerically, so `main` and
its literal `0x..` address count as equal): an equal pair is an empty ROI --
vsim would drain the instant it resumes -- and is rejected up front with rc=2.

> **Writing a kernel for cycle measurement (marker/PC modes):** keep the measured
> kernel anchored inside the `slti x0,x0,0x5A0/1` span -- read its inputs and
> write its outputs through memory inside the span, or wrap the kernel in a
> `__attribute__((noinline))` function called between the markers. The
> markers' `"memory"` clobber pins memory I/O but not register-only compute,
> so a kernel that carries live vector values in registers across the
> boundary may be hoisted/sunk out of the measured window. See
> `tests/fixtures/runtime/rt_c_helpers.h`.

---

## 4. Walk-through: one handoff in each mode

Each section is copy-pastable. They all share the same setup.

### 4.0 Common setup (do once per shell)

```sh
cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
source ./setup.sh                         # builds + exports env vars
make -C tests/fixtures -j        # builds .elf fixtures
```

Quick env check:

```sh
echo "$VSIM_QEMU"
echo "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
echo "$VSIM_BIN"
ls tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf
```

### 4.1 marker mode - the default (kernel)

Goal: run a vector fixture through QEMU1 -> vsim using the
two ROI markers (`slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1`) that the fixture already contains.

```sh
./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium
```

Expected output (stderr + stdout):

```
[andesim] model=hybrid engine=vsim:ax45mpv_premium vlen=<N> trigger=marker fixture=rt_c_v_matmul
[marker window_cycles] <N>  (vsim mcycle=<V> - qemu mcycle=<Q>)
PASS: --mode hybrid --trigger marker (rt_c_v_matmul)
```

The relayed output is just the program's own prints plus andesim's own lines:
vsim's startup banner (the `Copyright ... / Version :` lines) is stripped from
the vsim leg, the same as `cycle` mode, so the result stands alone. (vsim's
`[info]` log never reaches here -- the leg's stderr is dropped at capture.)

`./andesim run` orchestrates the two legs directly (no Python wrapper). Inside, the two legs are:

```
1) QEMU1 with -plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=$STATE
        -> drain at slti x0,x0,0x5A0   -> exit 200
2) sim_ax45mpv_premium $ELF \
        --resume-from-qemu $STATE --handoff-out $STATE_V \
        --shared-mem-path $SHM --shared-mem-size 128MB
        -> ROI runs in vsim, drains at slti x0,x0,0x5A1   -> exit 200
```

Try a different fixture:

```sh
./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_matmul.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium
```

### 4.2 PC mode - markerless workload, explicit boundary PCs

Same plumbing as marker mode, but the binary carries **no** trigger markers.
The user picks the switch PCs explicitly via `--pc-start` and `--pc-end`,
each a symbol name or `0x` address. Both args are required for `--mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium`.

Don't know where the hot region is? `build/hotloops` runs the binary
fast and reports the hottest loops (function, source line, PC range) as
an LLM-ready Markdown fact sheet. It auto-detects the QEMU binary,
plugin, and CPU from your build. Each loop block carries a `measure:`
field — a ready `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` pair that covers the enclosing
function entry to `ret` — that pastes straight into the command above.
`docs/andes_sim_gemm_tutorial.ipynb` walks that workflow end to end.

```sh
./build/hotloops --min-iters 10 my_kernel.elf
```

```sh
# resolve the boundary PCs once (cheap, host-side; needs HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ELF=tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf
START=vmatmul_kernel
END=$(${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN}/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump -d "$ELF" \
        | awk '/<main>:/{flag=1} flag&&/jal[[:space:]]+.*<vmatmul_kernel>/{getline; print "0x"$1; exit}' \
        | tr -d ':')

./andesim run "$ELF" --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --pc-start "$START" --pc-end "$END"
```

`rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf` is the **markerless twin** of the GEMM fixture,
built `-DHYBRID_MARKERLESS` from the same source as the marked
`rt_c_v_matmul`. Both triggers are one-shot (QEMU plugin `exit(200)` on
first match; vsim drains on first match), so the measured window is
**exactly one full `vmatmul_kernel` call** (16 outer rows + inner k-loop
+ vse32 stores). The cycle count should land near marker mode's ~22808.

The mechanism is fully general - pc mode can target **any** symbol or raw
address. `./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium` resolves `--pc-start` / `--pc-end` directly (symbol name or `0x` address) without needing env vars.

The underlying QEMU and vsim invocations (what the driver orchestrates):

```sh
# Resolve the boundaries (objdump-based; pick any two PCs in the ELF):
OBJDUMP=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump
NM=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm
ROI_START=$("$NM" tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
              | awk '$3=="vmatmul_kernel"{print "0x"$1}')
ROI_END=$("$OBJDUMP" -d tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
              | awk '/<main>:/{flag=1} flag&&/jal[[:space:]]+.*<vmatmul_kernel>/{getline; print "0x"$1; exit}' \
              | tr -d ':')
echo "enter=$ROI_START  exit=$ROI_END"   # e.g. 0x10021c / 0x1002cc

# QEMU1 leg
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=/dev/shm/share,size=134217728 \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -bios tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=/tmp/q1.bin,enter_pc=$ROI_START"

# vsim leg
"$VSIM_BIN" tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
  --resume-from-qemu /tmp/q1.bin \
  --handoff-out /tmp/v.bin \
  --shared-mem-path /dev/shm/share \
  --shared-mem-size 134217728 \
  --hybrid-exit-pc "$ROI_END"
```

The fixture binary differs from marker mode (markerless vs marked), and the
QEMU1 plugin and vsim flags carry hex PCs (`enter_pc=` / `--hybrid-exit-pc`)
instead of marker-trigger plumbing.

### 4.3 Capturing a Kanata pipeline trace of the ROI

When debugging a hot path on vsim, pass `--kanata FILE` to `./andesim run`
in marker or pc mode. The resulting trace contains pipeline records only
for the ROI region (between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain) -- vsim
boot and DMI resume overhead are filtered out.

```sh
# marker mode: the ROI is the span between the two ROI markers (slti x0,x0,0x5A0/1)
# markers already in the source. vsim auto-derives the window.
./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf \
  --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata

# pc mode: the ROI bounds are whatever PCs you passed.
./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
  --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x1002cc \
  --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata
```

Add `--objdump FILE` so the kanata `L` records embed the disassembly
text next to each PC. Generate the dump once with the toolchain
`objdump -d`:

```sh
$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump -d \
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf > /tmp/roi.S
./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf \
  --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata --objdump /tmp/roi.S
```

Open `/tmp/roi.kanata` in [Konata](https://github.com/shioyadan/Konata)
to view the pipeline.

Constraints:

- `--kanata` is only valid with `--mode hybrid --trigger marker` or `--mode hybrid --trigger pc` (the only triggers with a single ROI-exit PC); any other trigger is rejected with rc=2.
- marker mode requires exactly one `slti x0,x0,0x5A1` (exit marker) in the
  ELF. If the binary has more than one, vsim errors out with
  `multiple ... markers in ELF -- use \`--mode hybrid --trigger pc\` with explicit \`--pc-end\``.
  Switch to pc mode and pick the desired exit explicitly.
- `--objdump` requires `--kanata`.

How it works:

- `./andesim` appends `--kanata FILE --kanata-roi`
  (and `--objdump FILE`) to vsim's argv.
- vsim's `--kanata-roi` flag defers the kanata enable until after
  `--resume-from-qemu` loads the input state and `enable_hybrid_handoff`
  scans the ELF, then derives a one-shot `LoopGate`:
  - `start_pc` = the resumed PC (where vsim first fetches user code)
  - `end_pc`   = `--hybrid-exit-pc` (pc mode) or the unique
    `slti x0,x0,0x5A1` PC from CsrTrigger (marker mode)
  - `skip_iters=0`, `record_iters=1` (open on first fetch of start_pc,
    close on first retire of end_pc).

### 4.4 Verifying a hybrid run against a QEMU oracle (`--verify`)

With the QEMU2 handback removed, the code after your ROI never runs, so a
hybrid run normally proves only that a cycle figure came out. `--verify`
(default OFF) cross-checks the run's correctness:

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --verify your_prog.elf
# ...
# [marker window_cycles] 46  (vsim mcycle=... - qemu mcycle=...)
# [state-diff] PASS: 109 fields match (counters and passthrough CSRs excluded)
# [verify] PASS: vsim drain matches the QEMU oracle
```

Performance note: without `--verify`, the vsim leg drains only `mcycle`/`minstret`
(the cycle figure) and skips reading back the full architectural register file
over the Debug Module. A full drain reads every GPR, FPR, and transported CSR
with one Abstract Command each (only the vector registers ride a Program-Buffer
sweep through the shared scratch page); those simulated debug cycles dominate
hybrid wall-clock for a short ROI but never affect the cycle count -- the
counters are read before the rest of the drain. `--verify` needs every field
for the diff, so it keeps the full drain; expect a `--verify` run to take
noticeably longer than the same run without it.

How it works: after the normal run, the same ELF re-runs on pure QEMU (the
oracle) with the plugin draining at the ROI exit boundary, sampled at the
exact pc where vsim halted. The pre-ROI path is QEMU in both runs, so the
ROI inputs are identical -- any architectural divergence inside the ROI
(RTL bug, state-restore bug, drain bug) shows up as a field mismatch and
the run exits non-zero, listing each differing field:

```
[state-diff] x10: ref=0x3d got=0x0
[state-diff] FAIL: 1 mismatch(es) (115 fields compared)
```

What is compared: pc, all GPRs, all FPRs (when FP state is live), the V
CSRs and full vector registers (when V state is live), and the writable
M-mode CSRs that round-trip through the handoff -- `mscratch` (L23) and
`mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie` (L24), restored at resume and re-read at
drain. What is not:

- `mcycle`/`minstret` -- the engines count differently by design;
- `mip` -- restored and re-read, but its pending bits are hardware-driven
  (the timer bit tracks elapsed time, which differs between QEMU's
  functional clock and vsim's cycle clock), so a compare would
  false-positive;
- `mstatus`, `mtvec` -- passthrough: vsim restores the QEMU1 entry snapshot value; both sides hold the same bits by construction so comparing is trivially true but not useful;
- `satp`, `medeleg`/`mideleg` -- S-mode CSRs, not implemented on the default M-only engine. The privilege level itself IS compared: both
  sides drain the real one (L6), so a wrong-privilege resume shows up as
  a priv mismatch.

The handoff also carries the **v6 write-mask**: the plugin tracks which config
CSRs (the Andes block, PMA, the M-ext block, `mcache_ctl`/`mmisc_ctl`) your
program actually WROTE, and the cycle engine restores -- and `--verify`
compares -- only those. A CSR the program never touched keeps the engine's own
reset value instead of inheriting QEMU's reset default, so reset-value
differences between QEMU and any engine cannot skew the run. The tracking is
translation-time work in the plugin (only CSR-write instructions get a
callback), so the fast leg's speed is unaffected.

The write-mask also powers an **incompatibility warning** on every hybrid run
(not just `--verify`): if your program wrote a config CSR the chosen cycle
engine does not implement, the driver prints

```
[andesim] warning: the program wrote CSRs engine vsim:<engine> does not
implement: <names> (on this engine's silicon these writes would trap; the
hybrid restore skipped them)
```

to stderr. On that engine's real silicon the `csrw` would trap before the ROI,
so the cycle figure may not represent this program on this engine -- pick an
engine that implements those CSRs, or drop the writes. A clean run prints
nothing.

The handoff also carries the **v5 L2C block**: the L2 cache controller's MMIO
register window (0x0000..0x0527, base 0xE0500000). This is device MMIO, not a
CSR -- the QEMU plugin reads the window by physical address, and vsim writes back
only the writable boot-static config registers (Control 0x0008 = `CEN` enable +
prefetch + ECC + RAM timing, HPM Control, Way Allocation Masks) via
Program-Buffer stores before resuming. It is the L2 analog of the L1 `mcache_ctl`
transport and matters for the cycle figure the same way: an L2-enabled engine
that resumed with L2 disabled would run the ROI severalfold slower. Restore is
gated on the cycle engine actually having an L2C (`NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB > 0`);
every engine shipped today is built without one, so the block rides
forward-looking and no-ops. `--verify` compares the Control Register (masking the
read-only INITSTATUS bit).

The handoff also carries the v3 Andes block (`mxstatus`, ILM/DLM bases, PMA, ...)
and the **v4 M-ext block** (`HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST`): the writable M-mode CSRs
across the whole AndeStar V5 SPA -- perf counters, NMI, CLIC, trap-save,
state-enable, debug triggers, ePMP, CCTL, peripheral bases, U-mode Andes control
(51 CSRs). Every one is **capability-gated by CSR address**: an engine restores,
drains, and `--verify`-compares only the CSRs its config implements (reported via
`--describe andes_csrs`), so a CSR the core lacks is a no-op rather than a DM
hang. On the default `ax45mpv_premium` (M-only) that gates on the perf-monitor +
trigger CSRs; the rest ride forward-looking for a CLIC / Smrnmi / Smstateen /
M+U-capable engine. A few supported-but-engine-divergent CSRs are transported and
restored but excluded from `--verify` (like `msp_bound`): the HW perf counters
`mhpmcounter3-6`, `mdcause`, the trigger defaults `tdata1`/`tcontrol`, and the
ILM/DLM base+enable CSRs `milmb`/`mdlmb` (their enable bit reads 1 on the vsim
RTL but 0 on QEMU, which models no local memory). The
complete per-CSR disposition for all 232 spec CSRs is in
`docs/csr_coverage.ipynb`, guarded against drift by
`tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py`.

Per-engine CSR validation is a registration requirement: every supported
engine build carries its own CSR manifest + registration report under
`tests/engines/` (contract: `tests/engines/README.md`). For a human-readable
answer to "which CSRs does this engine restore, and under which condition --
or why not", read the engine's `csr_restore_table.md` in the same directory
(generated from the manifest by `tests/engines/render_restore_table.py`;
`test_restore_table.sh` guards it against drift).
`docs/engine_registration_tutorial.ipynb` walks the whole lifecycle --
the three-way audit (spec x config.inc x RTL), registering a new engine or
config, and removing one. `docs/csr_transport_bringup_tutorial.ipynb` is the
companion reference: what the `/csr-transport-bringup` skill does (its 7-phase
pipeline), every column of `csr_manifest.csv`, and each file a registration
ships under `tests/engines/<engine>-<confighash>/`.

Costs and limits: the oracle leg is one extra QEMU run of the whole
program (MHz-class -- cheap next to the vsim leg). `--verify` works with
`--trigger marker|pc`, assumes the single-shot ROI the hybrid run itself
assumes, and requires `--mode hybrid` (the other models have nothing to
cross-check).
